newsitem.title: JAPAN: E.Asia Grain - Japan, Korea to buy corn, wheat.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Grain - Japan, Korea to buy corn, wheat.

text.p: Japanese and South Korean importers are expected to pick up several more cargoes of corn and wheat this week to cover their needs for the last third of the year, dealers said on Monday.

The Japanese have covered only 20 percent of their U.S. corn needs for the last quarter and will buy more while Korean millers are tipped to buy a pair of 20,000-tonne wheat cargoes for September/October shipment and some 200,000 tonnes of corn.
"We'll buy U.S. corn this week. The firming U.S. Gulf/Japan freight rate partly encouraged us to cover now," a corn trader at a major trade house in Japan said.
Traders said offer prices of Chinese corn have gradually declined, but is still higher compared to U.S. origins. China is offering corn at US$130 per tonne C&F to Japanese buyers.
Corn premiums are currently pegged at 98 to 99 U.S. cents a bushel over CBOT September futures, they said.
In South Korea, buying is seen picking up sharply this week as buyers try to lock up supplies going into the last four months of the year, dealers said.
"We expect two major flour millers in Seoul would buy two 20,000-tonne cargoes of U.S. wheat this week for shipment between September to October," a dealer with a foreign trading firm said.
Korea's state-run Agricultural and Fishery Marketing Corp (AFMC) said earlier on Monday it would invite tenders on Saturday for 50,000 tonnes of corn to aid famine-threatened North Korea.
Delivery date was set for August to North Korea's western port of Nampo, near Pyongyang, an AFMC official said. Shipments would be made in lots of 5,000-10,000 tonnes each.
Traders said the corn was likely to be bought from China because it is near Korea and due to the need to transport the grain in a short period of time.
Another trader said the Korea Corn Processing Industry Association (KOCOPIA) were also expected to seek about 100,000 tonnes of U.S. corn for October arrival.

Another group known as the Top Margin Committee is also set to buy a 50,000-tonne cargo of corn for December arrival. The Committee had passed on tenders last week to buy 52,500 tonnes of corn due to higher-than-expected prices.

An official with the Pan Ocean Shipping Co Ltd said freight rates for July shipments of Panamax-sized cargoes from the U.S. Pacific Northwest were unchanged at $12.50-$13.00 a tonne over the past week.
Rates from the U.S. Gulf for Panamax-sized July shipments were also flat at $22 a tonne.
